quest.title: Daydreams Beyond Space and Time
quest.description: Garcia and company are preparing to return to Petrichor...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: ...We have to go, right this instant!

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: Calm down, Garcia. Didn't Officer Menthe say that things in Petrichor have returned to normal?

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: Sir, please, have faith in the good gentlemen of the Club. They are brilliant people, they will be fine, the threat notwithstanding.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Yes, yes, I know Babisse is very clever, and that Mécantre always has a strategy handy, but neither of them is good at dealing with malicious intent!

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: I sent them letters to warn them, but that despicable merchant was far too cunning for them!

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Ah! The humanity! Good folk are always being taken advantage of by the bad!

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: In that case, we can only put our faith in Mr. Bossuet, and hope that the Fontaine Research Institute can see the Club members through.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: See the Daydream Club itself blown sky-high, more like... Ugh...

choices.text: Looks like this is a job for me.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: #Ah, my dear {NICKNAME}, you're here at last! Wondrous, wondrous! Come, let us be off, immediately!

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: #Good to see you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. You've been doing well, I can tell.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey there, Kaia! Hehe, is it just Paimon, or did you get prettier since we last saw you?

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: Hmm, we do have a poem in Liyue. How does it go now? Something like...

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: I think I remember... "Even in fields a-flower, mine eyes dither to stray"... Something like that? It was in an anthology I read once.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Thank you, Lutong, Liyue truly is a comprehensive repository of poetic wonders! In which case, let us depart — in the name of said wonders!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're blushing.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: H—Hardly! I was simply... too warm! Yes! So worrisome were the wind and waves that I wore a few extra layers. Hahaha!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that so? Y'know, Paimon couldn't tell just by looking.

response.speaker: Menthe
response.text: Pfft. Alright, everyone, let's go. Everything is ready.

response.speaker: Menthe
response.text: My apologies, Mr. Garcia. I would have gotten you a few layers more if only we had known that you were so afraid of the cold.

response.speaker: Menthe
response.text: In that case, please head to Petrichor first. I'll be waiting for some colleagues here first, and we will join you shortly.

choices.text: I could pull it back down even if it does.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Ah... Petrichor! My homeland, how lovely, how familiar, how...

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: Quiet... Sir, is your hometown famed for its tranquility?

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Of course not. Babisse and Mécantre make all manner of crash and clamor every day, never mind anyone else...

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Wait... Mécantre, Babisse... We must go to the Club first. Come with me, quickly!

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: ...Was that real? Or just an illusion? I—I saw it...

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: I cannot tell either, but...
I... Wh—What have I done... Oh, Archons help us...

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Mécantre! Babisse! I saw what happened at the Club, and feared something must've happened to you! Where's Este? What about Grispan?

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: Garcia!? I must be dreaming... or have I always been? What brings you back here?

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: You're... Remuria... No, no, no! Archons, my mind's just filled with this stuff, isn't it...
You're... Garcia?

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: ...Grundeland. Just what are you up to this time? Find another opportunity to exploit? Or are you trying to take credit for our research again?

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: I... Well, I had considered doing so before, but...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ah, so this is the fellow who coveted your research?

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: That's right! That's him. He hired people to tail us, and even sent them to search my room, trying to take the Numbering Machine for himself.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: It hardly surprises me that you would wait for me in Petrichor once you realized that you wouldn't get anything out of me. I'll have you know, I already wrote a letter...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: One moment, Garcia. He doesn't quite look right...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Paimon would say that about everyone here, {NICKNAME}... C—Could it be that...

choices.text: (Aye, it's the influence of Phobos.)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, you mean that they also had that dream and became... other Remurians too?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Just like Este.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: R—Right. If they've been on this island the whole time, then Phobos would have...

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: I... That was exactly what I was thinking, Garcia. I confess, I was once an awful villain, and I...

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: So, good sir, I assume you planned to lure him over to Petrichor, before using the noble sentiments of these friends of yours here to influence him?

choices.text: Seems like a smashing success, if you ask me.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: I must say that had you demonstrated this talent in the past, our work would have gone much more smoothly.

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: Oh my... We might have to re-examine our relationship, Dear.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh...

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: H—Hang on, this isn't the time for jokes!

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: Ah, why was I so obsessed with control before? I... I truly am beyond help!

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Don't try anything funny, Grundeland. Mécantre and Babisse have already placed phonographs in town.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: All your dastardly ploys have been recorded, sure as we live. Babisse, Mécantre, you...

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: The phonographs? Oh yeah... I placed them. And then we took a walk and only talked about stuff to do with making money, truly silly stuff...

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: Investment, stock ownership, promotion... Mora, Mora, Mora rolling everywhere, all while our minds filled up like giant waterbags...

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: But wait... Where did I put them? Do you remember, Babisse?

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: In the, uh, flower pots? The one in the town? Next to the bell? The hall, the stone statue, the hall... and with Mr. Bossuet... Wait, where's he gone?

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: ...Sir, there are no bells in this area, nor halls or stone statues. *sigh* Looks like there's no getting through to them...

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, please come with me as we search for the phonographs. I fear that is our only lead.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: Ms. Kaia, could I trouble you to accompany Mr. Garcia and these gentlemen here?

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: Leave it to me. They do indeed need some taking care of.

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: First, we need to find a way to calm them down...

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: Let me think. Hmm... A bowl of delicious hot soup would make for a good start.

choices.text: I didn't know you had a knack for this.
(Has Phobos's influence not faded completely?)

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: ...This research... big money... a pleasant collaboration. Trust me!

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: The Club's original purpose... provide for free... Research belongs to everyone...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: Work with me... provide to more people... Professional business channels...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: We can't convince everyone... lots of research results...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: ...As long as you cooperate... I guarantee. First... maximum dividends...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: ...Become the wealthiest researcher... Research whatever you want...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: Prerequisite... get Garcia... original data...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: ...Stupid researchers... not even a ten-thousandth of your intelligence...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: Cooperation... Mora... big business... doesn't work out, we'll just have to make him suffer some...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: ...Contract is here... sign here...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: ...Huh!? What's... happening...

dialogues.speaker: Choppy, Broken Recording
dialogues.text: (A few dull thuds can be heard from the phonograph, and afterward, no more speaking can be heard.)

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: Thank you, kind lady... But I'm still feeling quite dizzy...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: See? I told you it would work. They're looking much better already.

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: In that case, you should take the opportunity to recover.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Before the Gardes come to recover you, at any rate.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right, that's right! We've got evidence proving that you're a bad guy right here!

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Thank Petrichor, you're back! Did you get those phonographs?

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: Of course, sir. Our plan worked. Babisse recorded this all-too-clever fellow's words down in full. It's all here in the phonographs.

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: You... You misunderstand. I shan't deny that I did terrible deeds in the past. I'm a scoundrel, rotten to the bone! I simply wish to redeem myself!

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: ...Ms. Kaia, did you put some kind of special Sumeru shrooms in your soup? You know, the sort that might make people want to turn their lives around in the blink of an eye?

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: No, I just made a pot of some simple fish soup. No spices, either, just salt.

choices.text: Your charms appear most potent.

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: Thank you, though... I suspect such charms as I have would only work on one person.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: What are you up to this time, Grundeland? I've warned you...

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: The Daydream Club's research will not be used to make a single Mora! We are researchers, not money-grubbing louts!

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Garcia, please wait... I... I'm willing to put a little faith in his desire to better himself.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: I agree. We should at least give him a chance.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: Alright, it seems that things are getting complicated. Let us take all of you to see a doctor first, shall we?

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: No, no, Garcia, listen to me. We... We experienced a huge collective dream.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: In said dream, we had turned into stone statues, yet we weren't fully so. We could still think, see, and hear.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: I could feel that someone else was in that stone statue besides me.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: I could see through his eyes and hear through his ears, and think along with him through his soul... I was him, yet not him!

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: Me too... I felt that the person with me was a good person full of ideals and intelligence, who was constantly doing research and work, though not for himself.

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: He was following someone as a musician does a conductor's baton, but he never once noticed it. What... a terrifying life to have led. Ohhh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh oh, {NICKNAME}. When he says "conductor's baton," do you think he means...

choices.text: The Grand Symphony that governed Remuria...

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: #Dear {NICKNAME}, what are you talking about? Please, for this town's sake, do continue to be our bastion of normalcy!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I know where their symptoms come from.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You do your best to describe Remuria and Phobos in the simplest terms possible...

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: ...So you mean to say that our dreams were real, and no illusion?

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: #It is hard to believe, but your explanation does make sense, {NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Remuria? B—But... That is a city that exists only in legend. And even if it existed, that must have been... hundreds of years ago now? I cannot recall...

choices.text: It's a real place. I've been there.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: ...Were it anyone else, I would have thought them mad. But you have always been truthful, so I will trust you.

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: You have been there!? It really exists!? Good gods! Take me there! Please! I must go!

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Me too! I... I must see that stone statue!

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: Me too! I must go see him!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It is incredibly deep underwater...

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: Not to worry. We have plenty of divesuits at the Club, more than enough to get us all down there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, is your place a club or some kinda treasure vault? What don't you have in there?

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: These divesuits are there thanks to dear Mr. Grispan. He bought them to study underwater hypnotism.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: I wish him health, no matter where he is.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Anyway! Enough chit-chat. I'm coming with you all. I, for one, do not believe that Grundeland will change so easily.

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: In that case, I suppose I'm coming too.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Kaia, it's dangerous down there. You...

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: Oh, believe you me, dear, you're not half as skilled as I. Lutong, are there enough suits to go around?

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: I counted, milady. Even counting all of us, there are more than enough divesuits.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: If for any reason you happen to lack one, then my suit will go to you. I'm quite talented at diving without equipment.

choices.text: Is there anything you're not talented at, Lutong?

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: Hmm... That depends on how you'd define the term.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: #Alright. I suppose our expedition team has been formed. As for who shall take the lead, I believe you to be the best choice, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: Follow close once we're underwater.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: #We shall obey your directions, then, {NICKNAME}.

choices.text: If you wander about, you'll end up in the Vishap King's belly.
Where in Liyue did you learn that?

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: #Hahaha, {NICKNAME}, my teacher was the roaring sea, and my growling stomach. The latter taught me quite a few things, too.

choices.text: It's underwater. I have witnessed its symphony.
As we thought, they were affected by Phobos.
This must be Petrichor's natural charms at work.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, this town's pretty, sure, but not that pretty...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: I never imagined that my first diving trip would be in search of a city I glimpsed in a dream. How fascinating.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: True, and one that has been sundered from the present for who knows how long, at that. It should have long since been buried in time...

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: ...Though we haven't found that city yet, this... bell is making quite the impression already.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Babisse, do you find anything around here familiar?

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: No, sorry... We were in a certain room at that time, and we couldn't move at all.

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: Just like stone statues.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Stone statues? But according to you, those statues had a different consciousness within them, right? So you were like...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: Like the statue's shadow, transcending time, space, and dreamscapes alike... Ah, a shame that I did not have that dream myself.

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: Milady, if you had turned into a statue's shadow, I fear Mr. Garcia and I would have no choice but to interview every stone in Fontaine.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: *cough* Anyway, let's continue onward for now and look for your statue, alright, Mécantre?

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: ...It's right there! Up ahead! I remember now. I passed this way!

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Hey, hey, Grundeland! Stop right there, you dratted—!

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}! Please go with Mécantre and the others. I'll get a hold of Grundeland!

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: Yes, Sir. I will keep an eye on Ms. Kaia... As I would have, even if you had not managed to ask me to in time.

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: #Pfft... Nice to see that he's in such high spirits. In that case, {NICKNAME}, let us go on ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: With any luck, Mécantre's statue won't be too hard to find.

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: ...It's you. Yes, I know it! I dreamed of you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So this is...

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: That's right. In the dream, I was his "shadow."

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: He seemed to have been studying something known as a "high-altitude aqueduct." Even as a statue, he was constantly going over the details of its engineering.

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: How to lay it down across complex terrain, what materials to use, the length and width of said waterway...

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: That was what made him happy in life... He did not need to think of anything else.

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: And there I was, thinking about some strange aquabus design. It was... It was true happiness.

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: He was pondering an aquabus's specifications, style, and the time required to build it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, still together despite turning into statues? Guess you guys really are fated in some weird way...

choices.text: They're pretty passionate about their work, huh...

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: I respect their love for their research, but at the same time, I felt sad for them.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: I too, salute and mourn him.

choices.text: Is it because their research failed to bear fruit in the end?

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: No, nothing like that. There was just something missing in their research...

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Hey, everyone, could you lend me a hand? Grundeland's statue appears to have sunk and is tangled in seagrass.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: #We can't get rid of it ourselves like this. Could you help, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Is it because their research results proved to be flawed?
Par for the course for researchers, I reckon.

talks.objective: Return to the shore and talk to everyone

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: It's you... Yes, it's you. The person in my dream.

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: You... You were the director of the Remurian Academy of Sciences, in charge of all research projects. All was orderly, all went well, and it was true happiness...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Hang on a moment. Why are you all repeating the phrase "true happiness"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's nice liking your research and all, but most people wouldn't emphasize it as being "true happiness." There's... something creepy about all this...

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: But that's exactly what the person in the statue kept emphasizing to themselves, and they wholeheartedly believed in it.

choices.text: I see... So that's what they mean by a symphony that governs all.

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: He was a good man. Even after becoming a statue, he continued to worry about the other researchers, fret about unfinished research projects, and blamed himself for the latter...

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: But something was not right... and I just couldn't say what! And only once I'd awakened did Mr. Babisse tell me what was off.

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: They were so focused on research that they never once spared a thought for themselves!

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: This good person was just like all the others in their statues. They had no freedom. They just followed the invisible conductor's baton around.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you know that they didn't have any control?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. You didn't know about Phobos at first, did you?

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Well, we found something that they were missing.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: What they were missing was a "daydream." This is something that no researcher should lack.

choices.text: N—Nope, didn't get it!

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Of course. If a researcher's mind might be compared to a fast-flowing river, then the daydream is a reef or rock upon which the torrent crashes and upon which waves of inspiration spray.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Why can birds fly? Why do trees grow? Why does rain fall from the sky? Why does the world have color?

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Without such "daydreams," which simply come out of the blue, research would be as a pool of stagnant water.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: The "daydream" is the spark that every researcher is always pursuing but knows not how to grasp.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: The intelligence of these two researchers is not in doubt, but they never "daydreamed" a thing in their long lives, nor did they ever display the slightest curiosity about anything else.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: For example, as I heard them speak, I thought of at least three ways to slow water corrosion on aquabus hulls and two ways to improve its form.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: And then I began to think that, by combining the previously mentioned proposals, we could build a small boat that could speedily traverse the water.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: As for me, I was inspired by the detailing of their waterway construction, and I began to conceptualize a design that could be set between two mountains, creating a large bridge that could allow all kinds of large transports to pass through!

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: But they only researched waterways and aquabuses, and were utterly uninterested in anything else, nor did any other inspiration come to them. This is impossible for any researcher.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: And as you told us about what happened in Remuria, we finally found the answer to that mystery.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: These two researchers truly had "no control over themselves"... That is why we mourn them. That blind conductor's baton destroyed their inspiration, and ruined their research.

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: *sobs* I almost became that villainous conductor... Why... I'm not... I never was...

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: ...Err, could someone help me stop him from weeping in front of that statue?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh, Grundeland really does seem really sad...

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: Allow me to help, sir. This is no place for a talk, so I suggest we return to town.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: Do you two gentlemen wish to bring any souvenirs back?

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: No, we've taken more than enough.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What did you take? Are you lugging these statues back with you?

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: No, of course not. We're not taking anything nearly that heavy back with us.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: Good to see that you're in a good state of mind. Lutong, help me grab his arm so we can get him out of here. He's been weeping for so long that he can barely stand.

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, we shall be counting on you to lead the way.

choices.text: Is "daydreaming" really that important?
So this is how Phobos controlled people...

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: No, no, I'm not... I won't become the person who tormented you. No, never, never... *sobs*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He's... a real mess...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: To have seen someone's life in a dream, before returning to reality and understanding the pain that person went through...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: Then finding out that what you thought was a dream was, in fact, real, and the life you bore witness to was also real...

choices.text: It's almost as if you'd lived a second life.

response.speaker: Kaia
response.text: *sigh* I'll go make something to drink. Mind helping me out, Garcia?

response.speaker: Garcia
response.text: I'll be there. Lutong, watch over Grundeland, will you? If it turns out that his madness is an act...

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: In that case, sir, I will make it so he need not feign pain.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, you two look like you're doing just fine, Babisse, Mécantre.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: We've just seen many people in our line of work trapped in similar situations.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: Although this is the first time I've seen such... direct control.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: As to why Grundeland reacted so strongly, we have a theory that comes from a more... sentimental perspective.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: They say that the "despicable have their eyes closed." Grundeland used various methods to keep people under his thumb...

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: ...But he had never before taken note of or personally experienced what it was like to be controlled.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: This time, he was forced to experience that pain for himself.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: And the ordeal seems to have made quite the impression.

choices.text: He had no choice but to experience it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, by the way, you said that you'd already taken souvenirs with you. What did you get?

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: We memorized the results of the work of those two researchers, and we have decided to... follow in their footsteps, continuing their work along their lines of thinking.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: We're members of the Daydream Club — adding a dash of the fantastical to our research work is what we do.

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: Hahaha, you know what? I can't wait to design that little boat! I'll install the latest propulsion device in it, too, just you wait and see!

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: I'm going to borrow Garcia's Numbering Machine in a bit to calculate the various parameters needed for that large-scale bridge... Yes, and we'll need to do a terrain survey, too!

response.speaker: Babisse
response.text: I hope those two researchers will enjoy our "daydream."

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: And if they don't, they're free to enter our dreams again. We can debate the matter then.

choices.text: "Daydreams" truly are a formidable power.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: As for me, once Mr. Grundeland is able to walk, I shall hand him over to Officer Menthe.

response.speaker: Lutong
response.text: I doubt she thought that a matter this complex would end this way...

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: I... *sobs* I'll never become that sort of... No, no, I already am!

response.speaker: Grundeland
response.text: *whimpers and cries*

choices.text: That's the Daydream Club for you, I guess.
I hope that impression will stay with him.

response.speaker: Mécantre
response.text: So do we. After all, not everyone can have such an experience.

choices.text: Let him rest.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: What has happened to the town? Did that idiot Grispan hypnotize everyone!?

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: But wait, where has he gone!? And he's taken Grobel with him, too... It couldn't really have been him, though, could it...?

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Please, Mécantre, Babisse, come to your senses! The Club is counting on you!

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: Calm down, Garcia. Let's go make them some soup first. A little something warm will help them recover their wits.

dialogues.speaker: Garcia
dialogues.text: Oh, alright... I really don't know what to do, Kaia. This is all a mess.

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Dear, it's alright. You've got me, and that's not in doubt, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: That's right. You just couldn't learn to "daydream"... There's no lack of reality all around us. You just lacked that power to dream...

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: You have to... We have to look up at the sky and cease obsessing over Mora and tall towers. An empty space is where a researcher truly belongs...

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: Ah, there is truly no hope for me... Why did I... Oh, Archons, why did I do those things...

dialogues.speaker: Grundeland
dialogues.text: I'm just like that person. I wanted to pull the strings. Let others do my bidding. No... No, no, no...

dialogues.speaker: Bossuet
dialogues.text: Fish... Ah, yes, that's right. This is the fish I discovered most recently...

dialogues.speaker: Kaia
dialogues.text: I only hope that we won't run into any trouble...

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: I hope so too, milady. As such, please stand behind us, and keep your distance from the water's edge.

dialogues.speaker: Mécantre
dialogues.text: The high-altitude waterway... What a wonderful idea... Yes, wondrous indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Babisse
dialogues.text: The aquabus... Your designs were exquisite. Of that I have no doubt.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The group quickly sets out on the road to Petrichor...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You and Garcia work together to move the statue onshore...

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: "Provide for free," hmm? Heh. A respectable virtue indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: It seems that he still hasn't figured out why the Daydream Club exists... A shame, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Lutong
dialogues.text: It appears evident that some accident occurred before they finished their conversation. A mixed blessing, as they say.
